summary: Tank kneels over Morpheus's body grieving him as a father and takes hold of the plug to unplug him, but Neo suddenly understands something and shouts "Stop!" He refuses to accept Morpheus's death as coincidence, recalling that the Oracle told him he would have to make a choice. Neo announces he is going into the Matrix to rescue Morpheus. Trinity protests that Morpheus sacrificed himself to get Neo out, but Neo confesses he is not the One, that the Oracle told him so too, and that Morpheus is the one who matters. Tank argues the rescue is suicide against three Agents in a military building, but Neo admits he cannot explain it logically and says he has to go because he now believes in something: that he can bring Morpheus back. Trinity, moved, climbs into the chair beside him to join him. When Neo says she is not coming, she asserts that as the ranking officer she is coming and orders Tank to load them up.

what_changes.before: Paralyzed by the finality of the moment, accepting that Morpheus must die.
what_changes.after: Sees it "perfectly clear" that he must make a choice and act to save Morpheus.
what_changes.evidence: Neo suddenly sees it perfectly clear, fate

what_changes.before: Believing Morpheus died to protect him as the prophesied One.
what_changes.after: Rejecting that he is the One and committing to risk his life for Morpheus instead.
what_changes.evidence: I'm not the One, Trinity. The Oracle

what_changes.before: Uncertain and questioning: "This can't be mere chance. It can't be! Can it?"
what_changes.after: Certain and self-defining: he believes he can bring Morpheus back.
what_changes.evidence: Because I believe in something. ... I believe I can bring him back.

what_changes.before: Unable to watch and trying to stop Neo from going back in.
what_changes.after: Climbing into the chair beside him to join the rescue.

what_changes.before: Preparing to pull the plug and kill Morpheus to protect Zion.
what_changes.after: Ordered to load Neo and Trinity up to attempt the rescue instead.

event_hint.kind: a wake interrupted by a decision
event_hint.one_line: During the crew's mourning of Morpheus, Neo halts the plan to unplug him and decides to go back into the Matrix to rescue him, with Trinity joining him.

minds.wants: To stop the crew from killing Morpheus and to go back into the Matrix to rescue him, overriding their logic and their grief.
minds.feels: A sudden, almost physical certainty has replaced his paralysis — fate feels like an oncoming train, and the Oracle's words ('you would have to make a choice') have snapped into meaning. Underneath the conviction is a deeper turn: he has stopped trying to be the One and is now willing to die for a man, not for a prophecy. His 'I believe I can bring him back' is not a tactical assessment but a leap of faith he admits he cannot justify logically.
minds.shows: Outrage and urgency — 'Goddamnit!', the sharp 'Stop!', the refusal to argue on Tank's terms. He is blunt about not being the One, almost dismissive of his own importance ('just another guy'), and offers no plan, only belief. He tries to exclude Trinity ('No you're not').
minds.basis: The text marks a concealment and a turn explicitly: 'Neo suddenly grasps the truth, destiny charging toward him like a speeding locomotive.' and 'Neo is frozen, his entire existence halted by the crushing weight of this instant.' His dialogue moves from 'Can it?' (uncertainty) to 'I believe I can bring him back' (certainty), and he confesses 'I'm not the One' to Trinity. He admits he 'can't logically explain' why the suicide mission isn't suicide.

believes_about.belief: Morpheus died for a mistaken faith — he bet his life on Neo being the One, and Neo now thinks that bet was wrong and that Morpheus, not he, is the one who matters.
believes_about.wrong_because: Neo is certain the prophecy is false and that Morpheus wasted himself on an error; the coming events will treat Neo's own unacknowledged capability as the thing that actually pulls the rescue off, so his self-dismissal is a misreading of himself, not just of the prophecy.

believes_about.belief: Trinity needs him to be the One, and that her devotion is to the prophecy rather than to Morpheus or to Neo himself — which is why he tries to keep her out of the rescue.
believes_about.wrong_because: Trinity explicitly reverses this: she says Morpheus means more to her than to Neo and acts from her own will and rank, not from any dependence on Neo's prophesied status.

minds.wants: First to stop Neo from throwing his life away; then, once she cannot, to seize control of the mission so she is the one determining whether Morpheus is reached.
minds.feels: She is gutted — she couldn't bear to watch the plug pulled and her tears fall freely — and then stunned when Neo says he isn't the One ('No, you... have to be'). Her need for Neo to be the One is a private article of faith, and when she tries to explain why, 'uncertainty swallows her words' and she cannot say it. That collapse of certainty is what frees her to convert her grief into action rather than remain frozen.
minds.shows: She protests on practical and moral grounds ('Morpheus gave his life to rescue you'), then, after a beat of silence, her jaw sets and she climbs into the chair. She drops all appeal and issues a rank-order ultimatum, complete with 'go to hell,' ending with the command 'Tank, load us up.'
minds.basis: The text states the concealment directly: 'Doubt chokes her speech, leaving her unable to voice her desire.' It also states the physical turn: 'Trinity gazes at him, suspended over the precipice he just leaped from. Her jaw tightens and she begins to climb into the seat next to him.' Her 'No, you. have to be' and 'That's not true. It can't be true' show her investment before the pivot.

believes_about.belief: That Neo must be the One — so deeply that when he denies it she can only insist 'you have to be,' and cannot articulate why it cannot be otherwise.
believes_about.wrong_because: Marked by the text as a belief she cannot defend in the moment; whether it is wrong about Neo is the question the following events will answer, and her inability to voice her reason is the drama of it.

believes_about.belief: That Neo's refusal to let her come is because he doesn't value Morpheus as she does or can't handle the mission — the premise she attacks with her 'let me tell you what I believe' speech.
believes_about.wrong_because: Neo's 'No you're not' comes from trying to protect her (and from his own lone-operator instinct), not from caring less; she reframes his protection as indifference to make her authority the deciding factor.

minds.wants: To do his duty by Zion — first by ending Morpheus's suffering and preventing the codes from being surrendered, then, once overruled, to serve the ranking officer's decision.
minds.feels: He is in mourning for both his brother (whom he has just covered with a sheet) and a man he calls a father, and he is being asked to perform the killing himself. His resistance to Neo's plan is the last stronghold of a grieving man clinging to logic against what looks like madness; beneath the 'loco' argument is someone who also wants Morpheus back ('I want Morpheus back, too') but can't reconcile that want with survival.
minds.shows: A eulogy, then a hand on the plug; then forceful, practical objections (military building, three Agents, suicide). When Trinity asserts rank, he stops arguing — the scene ends with him being ordered to load them up.
minds.basis: Continues directly from sc-146, where Tank draped his dead brother, explained the codes threat, and said 'We have to pull the plug' and 'we don't have any other choice.' Here he opens with the father-eulogy and takes hold of the plug, then argues the rescue is suicide while conceding shared desire for Morpheus. He offers no further reply once Trinity commands him.

believes_about.belief: That Neo is a frightened outsider proposing a suicidal fantasy born of denial, and that duty requires stopping him.
believes_about.wrong_because: Tank reads the mission through pure logistics and can't see the faith-based certainty that will actually carry it; his frame has no category for what Neo is becoming, which is exactly what the rescue will require.

minds.wants: Nothing legible here — he is unconscious and dying, the object over which the others decide.
minds.feels: Nothing readable; he is described as covered in cold sweat, mind being broken, body failing.
minds.shows: Nothing; he is inert while the others speak over and for him.
minds.basis: The scene treats him as a body being grieved and a plug being reached for; no reaction or decision is attributed to him. Inventing an interior life for him would be filling the field.

connects_back: sc-146: Tank's decision to pull the plug and his framing of Zion over Morpheus — Neo's 'Stop!' interrupts the exact action Tank began there.
sc-146: Tank draping his dead brother and calling Zion 'Zion outweighs me, you, or even Morpheus.' — grounds his grief and his duty-bound stance here.
Neo's earlier session with the Oracle ('you would have to make a choice'), now reinterpreted by Neo as the instruction he is finally acting on.
sc-145/sc-147: Morpheus being drugged and his mind broken for Zion's codes — the stakes (codes to the Zion mainframe) that make the rescue urgent rather than merely sentimental.
sets_up: ev-026: The crew's debate over the rescue's viability is now resolved into a decision to attempt it, with Trinity insisting on joining and taking command.
ev-027: Neo and Trinity breaching the government building and engaging its guards — made possible by Neo's decision to go in and Trinity's assertion of authority to come along.
ev-028: The helicopter assault to extract Morpheus — Neo's 'I believe I can bring him back' is the faith that the rescue will test.
ev-030/ev-031: Trinity's later confession of love to Neo and the subway showdown — the bond and belief between them forged here will be what she acts on when she is shot reaching the exit.
dramatic_function: This is the wake that becomes a decision: it converts the crew's mourning and fatalism into action by having Neo trade his anxious quest to be 'the One' for a simpler, more dangerous faith in a person, and by having Trinity convert her need for the prophecy into command. It reverses the scene's opening momentum (killing Morpheus to save Zion) and launches the rescue that defines the rest of the act.
